cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The new rule will ____ every student. (affect / effect)
cards.back: affect
cards.note: Verb meaning 'to influence'. 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning result: 'the effect of the rule'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Everyone ____ Riya has submitted the form. (accept / except)
cards.back: except
cards.note: 'Except' means 'other than'. 'Accept' means to receive or agree to.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The ____ addressed the school assembly. (principal / principle)
cards.back: principal
cards.note: 'Principal' is the head of a school; also 'main'. 'Principle' is a rule or belief.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The bus remained ____ at the signal. (stationary / stationery)
cards.back: stationary
cards.note: 'Stationary' means not moving. 'Stationery' means pens, paper and writing materials.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The soup and the bread ____ each other well. (complement / compliment)
cards.back: complement
cards.note: 'Complement' means to complete or go well with. 'Compliment' means praise.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ me what to do next. (advice / advise)
cards.back: advise
cards.note: 'Advise' is the verb. 'Advice' is the noun: 'good advice'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Be ____ about the matter; it is confidential. (discreet / discrete)
cards.back: discreet
cards.note: 'Discreet' means careful and tactful. 'Discrete' means separate and distinct.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She sought legal ____ before signing. (council / counsel)
cards.back: counsel
cards.note: 'Counsel' means advice (or a lawyer). 'Council' is an elected or advisory body.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Do not ____ your keys again. (lose / loose)
cards.back: lose
cards.note: 'Lose' (verb) means to fail to keep. 'Loose' (adjective) means not tight.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Do you need any ____ information? (farther / further)
cards.back: further
cards.note: 'Further' means additional. 'Farther' is used for physical distance: 'walk farther'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The dog wagged ____ tail. (its / it's)
cards.back: its
cards.note: 'Its' is possessive. 'It's' is the short form of 'it is' or 'it has'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She is taller ____ her brother. (then / than)
cards.back: than
cards.note: 'Than' is used in comparisons. 'Then' refers to time: 'first this, then that'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: ____ bag is this? (whose / who's)
cards.back: Whose
cards.note: 'Whose' shows possession. 'Who's' is the short form of 'who is' or 'who has'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: He was ____ the captain of the school team. (formally / formerly)
cards.back: formerly
cards.note: 'Formerly' means earlier or in the past. 'Formally' means in an official or proper way.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The teacher tried to ____ a response from the class. (elicit / illicit)
cards.back: elicit
cards.note: 'Elicit' means to draw out. 'Illicit' means illegal or forbidden.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The company is hiring more ____. (personal / personnel)
cards.back: personnel
cards.note: 'Personnel' means staff or employees. 'Personal' means private or individual.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ to the exit in an orderly manner. (precede / proceed)
cards.back: proceed
cards.note: 'Proceed' means to go ahead. 'Precede' means to come before.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: A storm is ____; stay indoors. (eminent / imminent)
cards.back: imminent
cards.note: 'Imminent' means about to happen. 'Eminent' means distinguished or well known.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The engineer found an ____ solution to the problem. (ingenious / ingenuous)
cards.back: ingenious
cards.note: 'Ingenious' means clever and inventive. 'Ingenuous' means innocent and frank.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The machine ran in a ____ stream all night without a break. (continual / continuous)
cards.back: continuous
cards.note: 'Continuous' means without a break. 'Continual' means happening repeatedly, with pauses.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She has ____ the loss with great courage. (born / borne)
cards.back: borne
cards.note: 'Borne' (from 'bear') means carried or endured. 'Born' means brought into life.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: They tried to ____ a plan to save water. (device / devise)
cards.back: devise
cards.note: 'Devise' (verb) means to plan or invent. 'Device' (noun) is a gadget or tool.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Take a deep ____ before you begin. (breath / breathe)
cards.back: breath
cards.note: 'Breath' (noun) is the air taken in. 'Breathe' (verb) is the act of taking in air.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: I wonder ____ it will rain today. (weather / whether)
cards.back: whether
cards.note: 'Whether' introduces alternatives. 'Weather' means the state of the atmosphere.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: We had ice cream for ____. (dessert / desert)
cards.back: dessert
cards.note: 'Dessert' is a sweet course at the end of a meal. 'Desert' is dry land, or to abandon.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ the book on the table. (lay / lie)
cards.back: lay
cards.note: 'Lay' means to put something down and takes an object. 'Lie' means to recline.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: ____ Hindi, she speaks French and Tamil. (Beside / Besides)
cards.back: Besides
cards.note: 'Besides' means in addition to. 'Beside' means next to.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: There are ____ students in class today than yesterday. (fewer / less)
cards.back: fewer
cards.note: Use 'fewer' with countable nouns (students) and 'less' with uncountable nouns (water).

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Please ____ that the door is locked before you leave. (assure / ensure)
cards.back: ensure
cards.note: 'Ensure' means to make certain. 'Assure' means to promise someone. 'Insure' is to cover with insurance.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The ____ for the new school has been chosen. (site / sight)
cards.back: site
cards.note: 'Site' is a location. 'Sight' is vision; 'cite' means to quote.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The sun will ____ at six tomorrow. (raise / rise)
cards.back: rise
cards.note: 'Rise' does not take an object. 'Raise' needs an object: 'raise the flag'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Of the two options, I prefer the ____. (later / latter)
cards.back: latter
cards.note: 'Latter' means the second of two things named. 'Later' means after some time.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: It is ____ cold this morning. (quiet / quite)
cards.back: quite
cards.note: 'Quite' means fairly or completely. 'Quiet' means silent.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'each', 'every', 'either' and 'neither' take which kind of verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb.
Wrong: Each of the players have a medal.
Right: Each of the players has a medal.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: a collective noun (committee, team, class) acting as a unit takes which verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb, with 'its'.
Wrong: The committee have made their decision.
Right: The committee has made its decision.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: after 'one of the' + plural noun, which verb is used?
cards.back:
A singular verb, because the subject is 'one'.
Wrong: One of my friends are a doctor.
Right: One of my friends is a doctor.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb. What is the exception?
cards.back:
When the two words together name one thing or idea, the verb is singular.
Wrong: Bread and butter are my usual breakfast.
Right: Bread and butter is my usual breakfast.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: with 'neither...nor' and 'either...or', the verb agrees with which subject?
cards.back:
The subject nearer to the verb.
Wrong: Neither the teacher nor the students was present.
Right: Neither the teacher nor the students were present.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: with 'as well as', 'along with' and 'together with', the verb agrees with which subject?
cards.back:
The first subject, not the phrase that follows.
Wrong: The teacher, along with her students, are going on the trip.
Right: The teacher, along with her students, is going on the trip.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'advice', 'information', 'furniture' and 'news' are uncountable. Can they take a plural form?
cards.back:
No. They have no plural and take a singular verb.
Wrong: She gave me many advices about the exam.
Right: She gave me a lot of advice about the exam.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: when is 'for' used and when is 'since' used?
cards.back:
'Since' marks a point in time; 'for' marks a period of time.
Wrong: I have lived here since ten years.
Right: I have lived here for ten years.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense goes with 'since' for an action that began in the past and continues?
cards.back:
The present perfect (or present perfect continuous), not the simple present.
Wrong: He is ill since Monday.
Right: He has been ill since Monday.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which form of 'be' follows 'wish' for an unreal present wish?
cards.back:
'Were' for all persons.
Wrong: I wish I was taller.
Right: I wish I were taller.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: what is the pattern of an unreal present condition (type 2)?
cards.back:
If + past tense, would + base verb; use 'were' for 'be'.
Wrong: If I was you, I will apologise.
Right: If I were you, I would apologise.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'a' or 'an' depends on what?
cards.back:
The sound, not the spelling: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.
Wrong: He waited for a hour at an university.
Right: He waited for an hour at a university.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which preposition follows 'different'?
cards.back:
'From', not 'than'.
Wrong: Her view is different than mine.
Right: Her view is different from mine.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: meaning 'talk over', 'be present at', 'go into', 'arrive at', do discuss, attend, enter, reach take a preposition?
cards.back:
No. In these senses they are followed directly by the object.
Wrong: We discussed about the problem.
Right: We discussed the problem.
cards.note: Other senses differ: 'attend to' (deal with) and 'enter into' (begin, e.g. an agreement) take a preposition.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'superior', 'inferior', 'senior', 'junior' and 'prefer' take which word before the second item?
cards.back:
'To', not 'than'.
Wrong: This phone is superior than that one.
Right: This phone is superior to that one.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: can a comparative or superlative be formed twice (more + -er)?
cards.back:
No. Use one form only.
Wrong: This book is more better than that one.
Right: This book is better than that one.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which pronoun case follows a preposition?
cards.back:
The objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
Wrong: The secret is between you and I.
Right: The secret is between you and me.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: items in a list must have what kind of form?
cards.back:
The same grammatical form (parallel structure).
Wrong: She likes reading, writing and to swim.
Right: She likes reading, writing and swimming.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'No sooner' is followed by which structure and which conjunction?
cards.back:
Past perfect (inverted) + 'than'.
Wrong: No sooner had he left when it began to rain.
Right: No sooner had he left than it began to rain.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'Hardly' and 'scarcely' are followed by which conjunction?
cards.back:
'When' (or 'before'), not 'than'.
Wrong: Hardly had she entered than the bell rang.
Right: Hardly had she entered when the bell rang.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'many a' is followed by which noun and verb forms?
cards.back:
A singular noun and a singular verb.
Wrong: Many a student have failed this test.
Right: Many a student has failed this test.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: distances, sums of money and periods of time treated as a whole take which verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb.
Wrong: Ten kilometres are a long distance to walk.
Right: Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: names of subjects like Mathematics and Physics, and 'news', take which verb?
cards.back:
A singular verb, despite the -s ending.
Wrong: Mathematics are my favourite subject.
Right: Mathematics is my favourite subject.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: how do 'the number of' and 'a number of' differ in verb agreement?
cards.back:
'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' takes a plural verb.
Wrong: The number of students are rising every year.
Right: The number of students is rising every year.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: a participle phrase at the start must describe which noun?
cards.back:
The subject of the main clause that follows it.
Wrong: Having finished the work, the lights were switched off.
Right: Having finished the work, he switched off the lights.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows a preposition?
cards.back:
The gerund (-ing form), not the infinitive.
Wrong: She is fond of to sing.
Right: She is fond of singing.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which pronoun case follows 'let'?
cards.back:
The objective case: me, him, her, us, them.
Wrong: Let he and I go.
Right: Let him and me go.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense follows 'It is high time'?
cards.back:
The simple past.
Wrong: It is high time we leave.
Right: It is high time we left.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which part of speech modifies a verb?
cards.back:
An adverb (usually -ly), not an adjective.
Wrong: She sings beautiful.
Right: She sings beautifully.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'would rather'?
cards.back:
The base form without 'to'.
Wrong: I would rather to stay home.
Right: I would rather stay home.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: how is the passive voice of the simple past formed?
cards.back:
was/were + the past participle.
Wrong: The letter typed by the secretary yesterday.
Right: The letter was typed by the secretary yesterday.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which preposition follows 'incapable'?
cards.back:
'Of', not 'to' or 'for'.
Wrong: He is incapable to telling a lie.
Right: He is incapable of telling a lie.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense shows an action completed before another past action ('by the time ...')?
cards.back:
The past perfect (had + past participle).
Wrong: By the time we arrived, the film started.
Right: By the time we arrived, the film had started.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The Speaker decided to ____ the member for unparliamentary conduct. (censor / censure)
cards.back: censure
cards.note: 'Censure' is to criticise formally; 'censor' is to suppress or cut parts of a text.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: He is so ____ that he believes every rumour. (credible / credulous)
cards.back: credulous
cards.note: 'Credulous' means too ready to believe; 'credible' means believable.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: We need a ____ judge, one with no personal stake in the case. (disinterested / uninterested)
cards.back: disinterested
cards.note: In its traditional sense 'disinterested' means impartial; 'uninterested' means not interested.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Drivers who ____ traffic rules should be fined. (flaunt / flout)
cards.back: flout
cards.note: 'Flout' is to openly disregard a rule; 'flaunt' is to show off.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The poem's last line is an indirect ____ to the Mahabharata. (allusion / illusion)
cards.back: allusion
cards.note: An allusion is an indirect reference; an illusion is a false impression.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The couple decided to ____ an orphaned child. (adapt / adopt)
cards.back: adopt
cards.note: 'Adopt' is to take on legally as one's own; 'adapt' is to adjust.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The club meets on ____ Sundays, that is, every second Sunday. (alternate / alternative)
cards.back: alternate
cards.note: 'Alternate' means every other one; 'alternative' means another possible choice.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She is my ____, and I tell her every secret. (confidant / confident)
cards.back: confidant
cards.note: A confidant is a person trusted with secrets; 'confident' means self-assured.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The police used tear gas to ____ the crowd. (disburse / disperse)
cards.back: disperse
cards.note: 'Disperse' is to scatter; 'disburse' is to pay out money.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Dense fog began to ____ the whole valley. (envelop / envelope)
cards.back: envelop
cards.note: 'Envelop' is a verb meaning to wrap or cover completely; 'envelope' is the paper cover for a letter.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: A ____ of fans rushed onto the field. (hoard / horde)
cards.back: horde
cards.note: A horde is a large crowd; a hoard is a stored-up supply.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: From the empty chairs we ____ that the meeting had ended. (imply / infer)
cards.back: infer
cards.note: To infer is to conclude from evidence; to imply is to suggest without stating.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: He was ____ to leave without thanking his host. (loath / loathe)
cards.back: loath

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The team's ____ was high after the victory. (moral / morale)
cards.back: morale
cards.note: 'Morale' is the confidence and spirit of a group; 'moral' relates to right and wrong.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The state will ____ the accused for fraud. (prosecute / persecute)
cards.back: prosecute
cards.note: To prosecute is to take legal action against; to persecute is to treat cruelly because of belief or identity.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: He is too ____ to criticism and is easily hurt. (sensible / sensitive)
cards.back: sensitive
cards.note: 'Sensitive' means quick to react or be hurt; 'sensible' means showing good sense.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Parliament passed a ____ to protect wildlife. (statue / statute)
cards.back: statute
cards.note: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature; a statue is a carved figure.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: We drove along a ____ mountain road full of sharp bends. (tortuous / torturous)
cards.back: tortuous
cards.note: 'Tortuous' means full of twists; 'torturous' means causing great pain.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: She doubted the ____ of his claim. (veracity / voracity)
cards.back: veracity
cards.note: Veracity is truthfulness; voracity is greed for food or knowledge.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The bank agreed to ____ the late fee. (wave / waive)
cards.back: waive
cards.note: To waive is to give up a right or requirement; to wave is to move the hand.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Candidates ____ for votes from house to house. (canvas / canvass)
cards.back: canvass
cards.note: To canvass is to seek support or votes; canvas is a heavy cloth.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The President gave his ____ to the bill, and it became law. (ascent / assent)
cards.back: assent
cards.note: Assent is formal agreement; ascent is the act of climbing up.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The listening test checks ____ comprehension. (aural / oral)
cards.back: aural
cards.note: 'Aural' relates to hearing; 'oral' relates to the mouth or speech.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: A ____ conference is held once in two years. (biannual / biennial)
cards.back: biennial
cards.note: 'Biennial' means once every two years; 'biannual' means twice a year.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The fugitive managed to ____ the police for months. (elude / allude)
cards.back: elude
cards.note: To elude is to escape from or avoid; to allude is to refer indirectly.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: A person with no sense of right and wrong at all is ____. (immoral / amoral)
cards.back: amoral
cards.note: 'Amoral' means lacking any moral sense; 'immoral' means breaking moral rules.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: Non-violence is a central ____ of Gandhi's philosophy. (tenant / tenet)
cards.back: tenet
cards.note: A tenet is a principle or belief; a tenant rents property.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The cyclone is expected to ____ havoc on the coast. (wreak / reek)
cards.back: wreak
cards.note: 'Wreak havoc' is the fixed phrase; to reek is to smell strongly.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: To ____ should the letter be addressed? (who / whom)
cards.back: whom
cards.note: Use 'whom' as the object of a verb or preposition: 'to whom'.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The law demands ____ treatment of animals. (human / humane)
cards.back: humane
cards.note: 'Humane' means showing kindness and compassion; 'human' relates to people.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The government issued an ____ because Parliament was not in session. (ordinance / ordnance)
cards.back: ordinance
cards.note: An ordinance is a law made by executive order; ordnance means military weapons and supplies.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: His rude remark at the meeting was most ____. (regretful / regrettable)
cards.back: regrettable
cards.note: 'Regrettable' describes what causes regret; 'regretful' describes a person who feels it.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Choose the correct word: The valley was covered with ____ vegetation after the monsoon. (luxurious / luxuriant)
cards.back: luxuriant
cards.note: 'Luxuriant' means lush and thick in growth; 'luxurious' means expensive and comfortable.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: what is the pattern of a real future condition (type 1)?
cards.back:
If + simple present, will + base verb.
Wrong: If it will rain, we will cancel the picnic.
Right: If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: what is the pattern of an unreal past condition (type 3)?
cards.back:
If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
Wrong: If she had studied, she would pass.
Right: If she had studied, she would have passed.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense follows 'when', 'before' or 'as soon as' for a future event?
cards.back:
The simple present, not 'will'.
Wrong: I will call you when I will reach home.
Right: I will call you when I reach home.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'has', 'have' or 'had'?
cards.back:
The past participle (gone, written, taken), not the simple past.
Wrong: He has went to Delhi.
Right: He has gone to Delhi.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'unless' already means 'if not'. What follows it?
cards.back:
An affirmative verb.
Wrong: Unless you don't work hard, you will fail.
Right: Unless you work hard, you will fail.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which auxiliary follows 'lest'?
cards.back:
'Should' (or the bare subjunctive), never 'will' or 'would'.
Wrong: Run fast lest you will miss the train.
Right: Run fast lest you should miss the train.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which conjunction pairs with 'neither', and which with 'either'?
cards.back:
'Neither' pairs with 'nor'; 'either' pairs with 'or'.
Wrong: Neither Ravi or his sister attended.
Right: Neither Ravi nor his sister attended.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: when a sentence begins with 'Not only', what happens to the word order?
cards.back:
The auxiliary comes before the subject (inversion).
Wrong: Not only she sings, but she also dances.
Right: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: when 'seldom', 'rarely' or 'never' begins a sentence, what happens to the word order?
cards.back:
The auxiliary comes before the subject.
Wrong: Seldom she visits her village.
Right: Seldom does she visit her village.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'used to' for a past habit?
cards.back:
The base form of the verb.
Wrong: She used to walking to school.
Right: She used to walk to school.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'such' or 'so' before 'a/an + adjective + noun'?
cards.back:
'Such'; 'so' goes directly before an adjective.
Wrong: It was so a beautiful day.
Right: It was such a beautiful day.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'too' suggests an unwanted excess. Can it replace 'very' in a happy statement?
cards.back:
No. Use 'very'.
Wrong: I am too glad to see you.
Right: I am very glad to see you.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'cannot help' (meaning 'cannot stop oneself')?
cards.back:
The gerund (-ing form).
Wrong: I could not help to laugh.
Right: I could not help laughing.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which tense goes with 'yesterday', 'ago' or 'last week'?
cards.back:
The simple past, not the present perfect.
Wrong: I have seen him yesterday.
Right: I saw him yesterday.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: can 'know', 'believe', 'want' and 'understand' be used in the continuous tense?
cards.back:
No. These stative verbs take the simple tense.
Wrong: I am knowing the answer.
Right: I know the answer.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: do the possessive pronouns 'hers', 'ours', 'yours' and 'theirs' take an apostrophe?
cards.back:
No. They never take an apostrophe.
Wrong: The red bag is her's.
Right: The red bag is hers.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which preposition goes with a date or a day: 'in', 'on' or 'at'?
cards.back:
'On' (on 5 May, on Monday); 'in' goes with months and years, 'at' with clock time.
Wrong: She was born in 5 May 2004.
Right: She was born on 5 May 2004.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: can 'despite' be followed by 'of'?
cards.back:
No. Say 'despite' or 'in spite of'.
Wrong: Despite of the rain, the match went on.
Right: Despite the rain, the match went on.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: do 'resemble' and 'marry' take a preposition before the object?
cards.back:
No. Both take a direct object.
Wrong: She resembles to her mother.
Right: She resembles her mother.
Wrong: He married with a doctor.
Right: He married a doctor.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: in a comparison, what must be compared with what?
cards.back:
Like with like; use 'that of' or 'those of' to avoid comparing a thing with a place.
Wrong: The climate of Shimla is cooler than Delhi.
Right: The climate of Shimla is cooler than that of Delhi.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'the poor', 'the rich' and 'the young' take which kind of verb?
cards.back:
A plural verb, because they mean groups of people.
Wrong: The poor is often ignored.
Right: The poor are often ignored.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'police', 'cattle' and 'people' take which kind of verb?
cards.back:
A plural verb, though they do not end in -s.
Wrong: The police has arrested the thief.
Right: The police have arrested the thief.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: how is a question tag formed after a positive statement?
cards.back:
A negative tag repeating the auxiliary and the pronoun.
Wrong: He is honest, isn't it?
Right: He is honest, isn't he?

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: what word order does a reported question use?
cards.back:
Statement order, with no 'do' support and no question mark.
Wrong: He asked me where was I going.
Right: He asked me where I was going.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: in 'There is/are ...', the verb agrees with which word?
cards.back:
The noun that follows the verb.
Wrong: There is many reasons for the delay.
Right: There are many reasons for the delay.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'had better'?
cards.back:
The base form without 'to'.
Wrong: You had better to leave now.
Right: You had better leave now.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: which verb form follows 'make' and 'let' with an object (active voice)?
cards.back:
The bare infinitive, without 'to'.
Wrong: The film made me to cry.
Right: The film made me cry.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: Rule: 'more than one' is followed by which noun and verb forms?
cards.back:
A singular noun and a singular verb.
Wrong: More than one student were absent.
Right: More than one student was absent.

cards.back: To supply something to a place that already has plenty of it; to do something unnecessary
cards.note: Example: Selling tea in Darjeeling is like carrying coals to Newcastle.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'unscrupulous' mean?
cards.back: Having no moral principles; unfair and dishonest

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'cross the Rubicon' mean?
cards.back: To take a decisive step that cannot be reversed
cards.note: Example: Once the contract was signed, the firm had crossed the Rubicon.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'uphold' mean?
cards.back: To confirm or support something that has been questioned, such as a decision

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'crocodile tears' mean?
cards.back: Insincere sorrow; a show of grief that is not genuinely felt
cards.note: Example: The rival shed crocodile tears at the minister's resignation.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'usurp' mean?
cards.back: To take a position of power or importance illegally or by force

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'cut the Gordian knot' mean?
cards.back: To solve a difficult problem in a quick, bold and decisive way
cards.note: Example: The chairman cut the Gordian knot by merging the two departments.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'vacillate' mean?
cards.back: To waver between different opinions or actions; to be indecisive

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a dog in the manger' mean?
cards.back: A person who spitefully prevents others from enjoying something that he or she has no use for
cards.note: Example: Don't be a dog in the manger; let others use the library room.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'draw a blank' mean?
cards.back: To fail to find or remember something
cards.note: Example: I tried to recall his name but drew a blank.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'vex' mean?
cards.back: To make someone feel annoyed, frustrated or worried

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'eat one's words' mean?
cards.back: To admit that what one said earlier was wrong
cards.note: Example: He had to eat his words when the team won the final.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'vilify' mean?
cards.back: To speak or write about someone in an abusively disparaging way

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a fair-weather friend' mean?
cards.back: A friend who is loyal only when things are going well for you
cards.note: Example: He vanished the moment I lost my job; he was a fair-weather friend.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'virulent' mean?
cards.back: Extremely severe, harmful or bitter in effect

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'flog a dead horse' mean?
cards.back: To waste effort on a cause or a matter that is already lost or settled
cards.note: Example: Arguing about last year's result is flogging a dead horse.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'vulnerable' mean?
cards.back: Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a fool's paradise' mean?
cards.back: A state of happiness that rests on false hopes or illusions
cards.note: Example: He lived in a fool's paradise, sure that exams needed no preparation.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'whimsical' mean?
cards.back: Playfully quaint or fanciful, especially in an appealing way

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'give someone the cold shoulder' mean?
cards.back: To treat someone in an unfriendly way by deliberately ignoring them
cards.note: Example: After the quarrel, she gave me the cold shoulder.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'wither' mean?
cards.back: To become dry and shrivelled; to fade or decline

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'go to the dogs' mean?
cards.back: To deteriorate badly; to be ruined
cards.note: Example: The old school has gone to the dogs since the new management took over.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'abysmal' mean?
cards.back: Extremely bad; appalling

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'have an axe to grind' mean?
cards.back: To have a selfish or private reason for being involved in something
cards.note: Example: The critic has an axe to grind against the author.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'acumen' mean?
cards.back: The ability to make good judgements and quick decisions

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'have a bone to pick with someone' mean?
cards.back: To have a cause for complaint that one wishes to discuss with someone
cards.note: Example: I have a bone to pick with you about yesterday's remark.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ameliorate' mean?
cards.back: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'in the nick of time' mean?
cards.back: At the last possible moment; just in time
cards.note: Example: The ambulance arrived in the nick of time.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'clandestine' mean?
cards.back: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'keep the wolf from the door' mean?
cards.back: To have just enough money to avoid hunger and poverty
cards.note: Example: His small salary barely kept the wolf from the door.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'cumbersome' mean?
cards.back: Large or heavy and therefore difficult to carry or use; slow and complicated

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'the lion's share' mean?
cards.back: The largest part of something
cards.note: Example: The lion's share of the budget went to defence.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'disdain' mean?
cards.back: The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's consideration or respect

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'make a mountain out of a molehill' mean?
cards.back: To exaggerate the importance of a minor problem
cards.note: Example: It's only a small scratch; don't make a mountain out of a molehill.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'dwindle' mean?
cards.back: To diminish gradually in size, amount or strength

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a necessary evil' mean?
cards.back: Something unpleasant that has to be accepted because it brings a needed result
cards.note: Example: For many workers, long commutes are a necessary evil.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'exorbitant' mean?
cards.back: (of a price or demand) unreasonably high

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'not to mince matters' mean?
cards.back: To speak plainly and frankly, without softening the truth
cards.note: Example: The principal did not mince matters about the poor results.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'inadvertent' mean?
cards.back: Not resulting from deliberate planning; unintentional

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'off the cuff' mean?
cards.back: Without any preparation; spoken on the spur of the moment
cards.note: Example: The leader's off-the-cuff remark caused a controversy.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'morose' mean?
cards.back: Sullen, gloomy and ill-tempered

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'on cloud nine' mean?
cards.back: Extremely happy
cards.note: Example: She was on cloud nine after topping the entrance test.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'ostracise' mean?
cards.back: To exclude someone from a society or group by general agreement

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'out of the woods' mean?
cards.back: Out of danger or difficulty
cards.note: Example: The patient is stable, but not yet out of the woods.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'recalcitrant' mean?
cards.back: Having an obstinately uncooperative attitude towards authority

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'pass the buck' mean?
cards.back: To shift responsibility or blame onto someone else
cards.note: Example: Officials kept passing the buck instead of solving the problem.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'relinquish' mean?
cards.back: To voluntarily give up or let go of something

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'pay lip service to' mean?
cards.back: To express support for something in words but not to act on it
cards.note: Example: Many companies pay lip service to equality without real change.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'renounce' mean?
cards.back: To formally give up a claim, belief or way of life

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'play second fiddle' mean?
cards.back: To take a subordinate role to someone else
cards.note: Example: He refused to play second fiddle to his younger colleague.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'replenish' mean?
cards.back: To fill something up again; to restore to a former level

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a red herring' mean?
cards.back: Something that misleads or distracts attention from the real issue
cards.note: Example: The clue about the gardener was a red herring.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'substantiate' mean?
cards.back: To provide evidence to support or prove the truth of something

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a red-letter day' mean?
cards.back: A specially memorable and happy day
cards.note: Example: The day of her graduation was a red-letter day for the family.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'vindictive' mean?
cards.back: Having or showing a strong or unreasoning desire for revenge

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'by the skin of one's teeth' mean?
cards.back: Very narrowly; only just
cards.note: Example: We escaped the flood by the skin of our teeth.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'conducive' mean?
cards.back: Making a certain situation or outcome likely or possible

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a snake in the grass' mean?
cards.back: A treacherous person who pretends to be a friend
cards.note: Example: Beware of him; he is a snake in the grass.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'contentious' mean?
cards.back: Causing or likely to cause an argument; controversial

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'sour grapes' mean?
cards.back: Pretending to despise something because one cannot have it
cards.note: Example: His claim that the prize was worthless was just sour grapes.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'discrepancy' mean?
cards.back: A lack of compatibility or similarity between two facts or accounts

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a stumbling block' mean?
cards.back: An obstacle that prevents progress or success
cards.note: Example: Lack of funds proved a stumbling block to the project.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'mandatory' mean?
cards.back: Required by law or rules; compulsory

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'take the bull by the horns' mean?
cards.back: To tackle a difficulty directly and boldly
cards.note: Example: She took the bull by the horns and confronted the manager.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'truncate' mean?
cards.back: To shorten something by cutting off the end

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'take someone to task' mean?
cards.back: To criticise or rebuke someone strongly for a fault
cards.note: Example: The editor took the reporter to task for the factual errors.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'spurious' mean?
cards.back: Not being what it purports to be; false or fake

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'tongue in cheek' mean?
cards.back: Said or done ironically or jokingly, not seriously
cards.note: Example: His praise of the weather was tongue in cheek.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'jovial' mean?
cards.back: Cheerful and friendly

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'turn over a new leaf' mean?
cards.back: To change one's behaviour for the better and make a fresh start
cards.note: Example: After the warning, he turned over a new leaf.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does 'resolute' mean?
cards.back: Admirably purposeful, determined and unwavering

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'turn the tables' mean?
cards.back: To reverse a situation so that one gains the advantage over a rival
cards.note: Example: The home side turned the tables in the second half.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'up in arms' mean?
cards.back: Angrily protesting about something
cards.note: Example: Residents were up in arms over the plan to cut the old trees.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'wash one's hands of' mean?
cards.back: To refuse to accept any further responsibility for something
cards.note: Example: I wash my hands of the whole affair.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'wear one's heart on one's sleeve' mean?
cards.back: To show one's feelings openly
cards.note: Example: She wears her heart on her sleeve, so everyone knows her mood.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'the writing on the wall' mean?
cards.back: A clear sign that something unpleasant or disastrous will happen
cards.note: Example: The falling sales were the writing on the wall for the firm.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a wolf in sheep's clothing' mean?
cards.back: A dangerous person who appears harmless or friendly
cards.note: Example: The friendly dealer turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'the salt of the earth' mean?
cards.back: A person who is admirably honest, good and dependable
cards.note: Example: Our neighbours are the salt of the earth.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a sitting duck' mean?
cards.back: A person or thing that is an easy target for attack
cards.note: Example: The unguarded ship was a sitting duck.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a skeleton in the cupboard' mean?
cards.back: A shameful or embarrassing secret that one tries to hide
cards.note: Example: Every old family seems to have a skeleton in the cupboard.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'look a gift horse in the mouth' mean?
cards.back: To find fault with something that has been given free
cards.note: Example: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth; just say thank you.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'at sixes and sevens' mean?
cards.back: In a state of confusion or disorder
cards.note: Example: The office was at sixes and sevens after the move.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'hand in glove' mean?
cards.back: In very close association with someone, often for a dishonest purpose
cards.note: Example: The contractor worked hand in glove with the inspector.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'head over heels in love' mean?
cards.back: Completely and uncontrollably in love
cards.note: Example: He fell head over heels in love with her at first sight.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'in a nutshell' mean?
cards.back: In a few words; briefly
cards.note: Example: In a nutshell, the plan failed because it was underfunded.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'a fish out of water' mean?
cards.back: A person who feels uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings
cards.note: Example: In the formal gathering he felt like a fish out of water.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'bear the brunt' mean?
cards.back: To suffer the main force of something unpleasant
cards.note: Example: The coastal villages bore the brunt of the cyclone.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'pour oil on troubled waters' mean?
cards.back: To calm a quarrel or a tense situation
cards.note: Example: The teacher poured oil on troubled waters by listening to both sides.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'smell a rat' mean?
cards.back: To suspect that something is wrong or that there is trickery
cards.note: Example: When the offer seemed too generous, I began to smell a rat.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'ride roughshod over' mean?
cards.back: To treat someone's wishes or feelings with arrogant disregard
cards.note: Example: The management rode roughshod over the staff's objections.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'blow hot and cold' mean?
cards.back: To keep changing one's attitude or opinion about something
cards.note: Example: He blows hot and cold about moving abroad.

cards.subject: english
cards.front: What does the idiom 'throw down the gauntlet' mean?
cards.back: To issue a challenge
cards.note: Example: The champion threw down the gauntlet to all newcomers.
